name: capsule-nav
summary: A floating capsule header that is edge to edge and transparent at the top of the page, then springs to a narrower, thinner frosted-glass pill once you scroll past a threshold, and opens out again on the way back. The narrowing is a real spring integrated per frame (stiffness, damping, mass), so a change of scroll direction carries its velocity instead of restarting a transition; only the glass itself fades in through CSS. Every size is a custom property. With no script the capsule rests edge to edge over the hero, which is the unscrolled look.

threshold.description: Scroll distance in px past which the capsule narrows and the glass fades in. Upstream's DEFAULTS.threshold.

damping.description: Damping c, about critical at 2*sqrt(k*m). Upstream's DEFAULTS.damping.

deviations.what: The UMD/IIFE wrapper, the DOMContentLoaded auto-init, initAll, the instances registry and the autoInit default are removed. The module exports mount(el, opts) and meta instead; mount finds the header inside the section with el.querySelector('.fx-cnav'), constructs the instance, and returns { update, destroy }. update() assigns the new options onto the instance and calls its update(); destroy() calls the instance's destroy(). The section carries data-fx-live while mounted.
deviations.why: Seam. Importing the upstream file assigns onto `this` and reads the document at load, which fails the no-globals-at-import rule and the DOM-less import test; an effect is mounted by the site, not by itself.

deviations.what: The two throws on a missing element or a missing .fx-cnav__bar / .fx-cnav__inner become the resting handle { update() {}, destroy() {} }, and mount() returns it first when handed no element, no document or no matchMedia.
deviations.why: Seam. A site mounts every effect it finds in one loop, and one throw would take the rest of the page's effects with it; the contract is that mount(null) survives.

deviations.what: Every --gnav-* custom property is --fx-*, and the classes gnav, gnav__bar, gnav__inner, gnav--dark and gnav--light are fx-cnav, fx-cnav__bar, fx-cnav__inner, fx-cnav--dark and fx-cnav--light, in both index.js (_readTokens) and style.css. is-scrolled is kept. Every value behind the renamed names is upstream's.
deviations.why: Seam. The effect contract prefixes custom properties --fx-, and the class names are ours so two effects never share a selector.

deviations.what: The data-gnav-threshold / -stiffness / -damping / -mass attribute overrides are dropped; threshold, stiffness, damping and mass are mount options, applied through the constructor's own merge over DEFAULTS and changeable through update().
deviations.why: Seam. Options are the contract's one configuration surface, and a second one read from attributes would let the markup and the registry disagree.

deviations.what: The demo page around the header is ours: the brand, links and call-to-action inside the capsule, the --fx-ink link colour, a font and ink colour added to upstream's .fx-cnav selector and a 20px horizontal padding added to .fx-cnav__inner (it stacks on upstream's pad-l-on / pad-r-on in the scrolled state), the tall two-tone section with a dot grid and two blurred colour blobs, and the hero and body copy under it. Upstream's index.html is a demo and is not ported.
deviations.why: Upstream ships only the header; a section needs a page under it tall enough to scroll past the threshold, something for the frosted glass to blur, and a resting frame that is not one flat colour.
